## Overview

`fit_limma()` fits a limma linear model to a numeric assay in a
`SummarizedExperiment`. Use `as_summarized_experiment()` to export one
ProteoVault measurement source and method. The assay has features in rows and
samples in columns; in-memory sample metadata becomes `colData`, which supplies
the experimental conditions for the design.

The default analysis converts positive intensities to log2 values, treats zero
as missing, fits `limma::lmFit()`, applies `limma::contrasts.fit()`, and
moderates variances with `limma::eBayes()`. It does not normalize, impute, or
select significant features automatically. See the
[limma User's Guide](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/limma/inst/doc/usersguide.pdf)
for the underlying statistical model.

## Prepare samples and one quantity assay

The metadata `sample_name` values must exactly match the vault. List the
stored names before preparing a mapping. The example below assumes a
`sample_info` data frame with one row per sample and columns `sample_name`,
`sample_id`, and `condition`.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(ProteoVaultR)

vault <- open_vault("P2042.proteovault.duckdb")
sample_names <- dplyr::collect(
    dplyr::select(tbl_vault(vault, "samples"), sample_name)
)
print(sample_names)

vault <- set_sample_metadata(vault, sample_info)
se <- as_summarized_experiment(
    vault,
    level = "protein_group",
    method = "PG.MaxLFQ"
)

table(SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)$condition)
SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(se)
close_vault(vault)
```

Choose one `source_id` when the requested method exists in multiple sources.
`as_summarized_experiment()` preserves the chosen source and method in its
metadata. A peptide-level assay is derived from precursor quantities and
requires an explicit `peptide_aggregation`; it is not a separately measured
peptide quantity.

## Label-blind stable-reference normalization

These functions select complete, abundant reference proteins without using
sample groups. Supply raw protein intensities and exclude prespecified target
proteins from reference selection. Each function adds a separate assay on the
original intensity scale, so `fit_limma()` can apply its usual log2 transform.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
se <- as_summarized_experiment(vault, level = "protein_group",
    method = "PG.Quantity")
se <- normalize_stable_reference_genorm(se,
    exclude = c("sp|P48426|PI42A_HUMAN", "sp|P78356|PI42B_HUMAN"))
se <- normalize_stable_reference_pca(se,
    exclude = c("sp|P48426|PI42A_HUMAN", "sp|P78356|PI42B_HUMAN"))

SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(se)
SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)$reference_genorm_log2_offset
SummarizedExperiment::rowData(se)$reference_pca_selected

plot_stable_reference_diagnostics(se, method = "genorm")
plot_stable_reference_diagnostics(se, method = "pca", style = "ggplot2")
```

The geNorm-style and PCA selections are alternative sensitivity analyses.
Their selected feature IDs and settings are stored in `metadata(se)`.

## Compare one treatment with DMSO

Suppose `condition` contains `DMSO`, `SBI-9456`, and other treatments. The
formula `~ 0 + condition` estimates one mean per condition. The contrast below
tests SBI-9456 against DMSO while retaining the other treatments in the model.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
se$condition <- factor(se$condition,
    levels = c("DMSO", "SBI-9456", "OtherTreatment"))

available <- list_limma_contrasts(se, "~ 0 + condition")
available

fit <- fit_limma(
    se,
    design = ~ 0 + condition,
    contrasts = c(SBI_vs_DMSO = "conditionSBI.9456 - conditionDMSO")
)

colnames(fit$design)
fit$contrast_matrix
head(fit$results)
```

The function makes design column names valid R names. Thus `SBI-9456` becomes
`SBI.9456` in a contrast. Check `colnames(fit$design)` if an expression does
not match. The contrast direction is treatment minus DMSO: positive `logFC`
means higher treatment abundance. Because the input is log2 transformed by
default, `logFC = 1` corresponds to a twofold difference.

For several comparisons, provide several named expressions. Each is tested
against the same fitted design, and the results contain a `contrast` column.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
fit <- fit_limma(
    se,
    design = ~ 0 + condition,
    contrasts = c(
        SBI_vs_DMSO = "conditionSBI.9456 - conditionDMSO",
        Other_vs_DMSO = "conditionOtherTreatment - conditionDMSO"
    )
)
```

## Interpret and inspect results

`fit$results` has one row per feature and contrast, in assay feature order.
`feature_id` matches the assay row name. It includes `logFC`, `AveExpr`, `t`,
`P.Value`, `adj.P.Val` (Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment within each contrast),
`B`, and available feature annotations. Protein-group members and mapped IDs
remain list columns; their many-to-many mappings do not duplicate tests.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
significant <- subset(fit$results,
    contrast == "SBI_vs_DMSO" & adj.P.Val < 0.05)
significant[order(significant$adj.P.Val),
    c("feature_id", "source_group_id", "logFC", "P.Value", "adj.P.Val")]
```

`fit$fit` is the moderated limma fit, `fit$design` is the exact design matrix,
`fit$contrast_matrix` records the comparisons, and `fit$settings` records
transformation and moderation options. The result includes all tested features;
the example threshold above is applied only for display.

## Volcano plots

`plot_limma_volcano()` displays log2 fold change against a transformed
probability axis.
It defaults to BH-adjusted q-values and the BPG style; select `"p_value"` for
unadjusted p-values or `style = "ggplot2"` for a ggplot object. Values are
positioned and labeled as `-log10(probability)`: `0`, `1`, `2`, and so forth.
There are no grid lines.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
plot_limma_volcano(
    fit,
    contrast = "SBI_vs_DMSO",
    significance = "q_value",
    proteins = c("O75083", "P12345"),
    label_by = "leading_gene_name"
)

plot_limma_volcano(
    fit,
    contrast = "SBI_vs_DMSO",
    significance = "p_value",
    style = "ggplot2"
)
```

`proteins` can contain exact feature IDs, complete protein-group names, group
member accessions or names, or mapped identifiers. One identifier can match
several groups, in which case all matching points are labeled. An unmatched
identifier raises an error. The legend title identifies the selected probability
type and shows `> cutoff`, `≤ cutoff; FC < 0`, and `≤ cutoff; FC ≥ 0`.
Points at or below `cutoff` (default `0.05`) are colored by fold-change direction.
Use `label_by` to display a character `rowData` column instead of the selected
accession. Selected features need a value in that column. Nearby labels are
placed at different heights to make them easier to read.
Annotated points are orange, drawn over the other points, and connected to their labels.

## Protein precursor profiles

`plot_protein_precursor_quantity_lineplot()` shows every linked charged modified peptide for
the selected proteins. Names on the protein vector become facet labels; the
quantification method chooses the precursor measurements.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
plot_protein_precursor_quantity_lineplot(vault,
    proteins = c(PIP4K2A = "sp|P48426|PI42A_HUMAN",
        PIP4K2B = "sp|P78356|PI42B_HUMAN"),
    method = "Precursor.Normalised")
```

## P-value histogram

`plot_limma_pvalue_histogram()` shows the raw p-value distribution for one
contrast. Both styles use equal-width bins from 0 to 1; `bins` controls the
number of bins.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
plot_limma_pvalue_histogram(fit, contrast = "SBI_vs_DMSO")
plot_limma_pvalue_histogram(fit, contrast = "SBI_vs_DMSO",
    bins = 20, style = "ggplot2")
```
Missing statistics are omitted; a stored probability of zero is drawn just
above the smallest positive probability so the plot remains finite.

## Input and design checks

- The selected assay must contain comparable measurements from one source and
  quantification method. Do not combine raw and normalized methods in one fit.
- With `log2_transform = TRUE`, zeros become missing by default; negative and
  infinite intensities are rejected. No pseudocount or imputation is applied.
- Set `log2_transform = FALSE` for an assay that is already on a log2 scale.
  Zeros are then retained unless `zero_as_missing = TRUE` is requested.
- The design must have one row per sample, full column rank, and residual
  degrees of freedom. Missing design variables cause an error.
- Missing feature values are passed to limma. Inspect feature coverage before
  interpreting a contrast, especially if one group has few observed values.
- `trend = TRUE` enables limma's mean-variance trend; `robust = TRUE` enables
  robust empirical Bayes moderation. Use them based on diagnostics, not as
  automatic defaults.

The same interface accepts `level = "precursor"` or a peptide assay exported
with an explicit precursor aggregation rule. These levels answer different
biological questions; a precursor result is not a peptide or protein result.
